newsitem.title: USA: Key panel upholds China MFN trade status.
newsitem.headline: Key panel upholds China MFN trade status.

text.p: The influential House Ways and Means Committee on Wednesday voted to uphold President Bill Clinton's decision to maintain normal U.S. trade relations with China and urged fellow lawmakers to reject a measure that would overrule the president.
The committee voted 34 to 5 to ask members of the full House of Representatives to reject a resolution that would revoke China's Most Favoured Nation trade status.

"If we cease our commercial relationship with China, we will have extinguished our ability to improve the human rights situation there," Ways and Means Chairman Bill Archer said. "Our presence in China assists in spreading our values and ideals throughout the country as well as benefitting the Chinese workers employed by our companies."

Supporters of maintaining normal trade ties with China argued it would be counterproductive for the United States to unilaterally withdraw MFN privileges. They said it would be better to shift the debate over relations with China away from commercial ties and toward issues of concern like human rights abuses, religious freedoms, missile sales and nuclear technology proliferation.
"This has no real value whatsoever," Rep. Robert Matsui, D-Calif., said of the annual debate on China's trade status with the United States.

MFN opponents urged lawmakers to put principle ahead of commerce. "We cannot accept what is happening in China," Rep John Lewis, D-Ga., said. "I believe in trade, free and open trade, but I don't believe in trade at any price."
